messages:
ava_cs: Heads-up: I put together a compact activation ops cheat-sheet for customer calls — quick rules for caching/batching/streaming + renewal flags. Posting here for feedback before adding to playbook. TL;DR at bottom. :memo:

liam_sol: Love it. Can you list the top 3 account health signals we should surface during onboarding?

ava_cs: Sure: 1) median latency per route rising >20% vs baseline; 2) % of calls hitting fallback model >5%; 3) active user-concurrency lower than expected (we map to usage tiers). Also track 'prompt churn' from customers. Short eq: Latency, Fallbacks, Usage.

priya_sre: Add: sustained cache-miss rate >30% for 24h window -> likely misconfigured prefixing/prompt variance.

ethan_csm: For renewal-risk flags: combine those signals with customer sentiment (cs notes) and unresolved enablement tasks older than 7 days. Score >=7 -> ops alert.

ava_cs: Below are practical ops steps to run on customer call: 1) Confirm sequence length distribution 2) Check token patterns for dynamic content 3) Validate KV/prefix cache keys 4) Suggest batching profile if tail latency OK

liam_sol: Can we add quick commands to show cache hit rates in telemetry?

priya_sre: Yes, telemetry query (example):
```
select sum(cache_hits)/sum(cache_requests) as hit_rate
from telemetry
where customer_id = 'ACME'
and ts > now() - interval '24 hours';
```

ava_cs: Also include a short customer script for 'activation checklist' to send pre-call: + sample prompt template to minimize variability. Example:
```
Prompt: "<system> You are a shopping assistant </system>\nUser: {user_query}\n"
Use placeholders not free text.
```

liam_sol: :thumbsup: I'll try this on the renewal call tomorrow. Any easy-to-share one-pager?

ava_cs: Draft one-pager link: https://redwood.internal/cs/activation-cheatsheet (WIP). I'll add a short checklist for handoff: preflight telemetry, config copy, shared prompt templates, next steps & owner.

onboard-bot: Reminder: Add entry to CS playbook for 'activation-cheatsheet' by EOD Friday. :robot_face:

ethan_csm: Nice. Can we capture customer feedback on the call via quick form? 3 Qs: Was latency acceptable? Did output quality meet expectations? Will you recommend us? -> Y/N + comments

ava_cs: Yes — I'll attach a short form and script. Thanks all. If no objections I'll merge into docs later today.
